structured.approach: I followed the data-science-steps DS-01 procedure. I read both inputs: feat.tasks, to find the lane's repository and tasks, and org.engineering_stack, for the stack, CI and Databricks facts. Shell commands are not permitted in this step, so I checked the repository by reading its git metadata (HEAD, branch refs, reflog, config) and source files (ci.py, __init__.py, predict.py, explain.py, tests/test_forecast.py, README, CLAUDE.md) with Read and Glob. The tool:repo-access view is the source for availability, write access and the clean working tree. Every statement about existing code cites the file that shows it. I removed the statement about the agent's allowed git actions, because the brief does not support it.

claims.text: The Data Science lane works in repository ap_forecast, on TSK-03 (STORY-03, vendor_risk) and TSK-04 (STORY-04, risk parameter on build_explanation_request).
Repository ap_forecast is available locally, and the agent identity has write access; git status is clean.
The checked-out branch is feature/story, created from dev at d67e866; dev and main point to the same commit.
No repository creation is needed; the origin remote points to GitHub repository arghya05/ap-forecast-sample.
No Databricks workspace or database is used by ap_forecast.
CI is /usr/bin/python3 ci.py and enforces line coverage of at least 90% plus static checks standing in for SonarQube.
The current ap_forecast version is 0.9.0, which matches feat.tasks section 2.
predict.py defines predict_delay_days; explain.py defines build_explanation_request and reads its provider and model from models.json.
tests/test_forecast.py holds test_predict, test_request_uses_config and test_request_with_explicit_config.
ci.py imports the third-party package coverage; whether it is installed was not verified in this step.

open_questions: RA-1 (non-blocking): the working branch is the generic feature/story rather than a story-specific feature/<story>, so TSK-03 and TSK-04 would share it. Confirm this is intended; the commit prefixes STORY-03 and STORY-04 keep traceability.
RA-2 (non-blocking): ci.py depends on the third-party coverage package. Confirm it is installed for /usr/bin/python3 at the first CI run (DS-06 or DS-07).
structured.summary: ap_forecast is available locally with write access, on branch feature/story created from dev at d67e866, with a clean working tree. No repository needs to be created, and no Databricks or database is involved. The files that TSK-03 and TSK-04 will change, and the folders their new files go into, all exist. task.repo_access is rewritten in full, with two non-blocking observations.
